sections.heading: Overview
content: The Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) provides continuous care to a critically ill neonate and involves many advanced technologies and interventions that are unique to the specialty area. These critically ill neonates can suffer from various medical conditions including congenital heart defects, neural tube defects, prematurity, respiratory distress, metabolic disorders and difficulties with feeding and growth. Diagnosis related groups (DRGs), including Medicare Severity Diagnosis Related Groups (MS-DRGs) and All Patient Refined Diagnosis Related Groups (APR-DRGs), are assigned to newborns based on factors including, but not limited to, birth weight, extent of prematurity, diagnoses, severity of illness, and associated significant problems. NICU is comprised of four levels of care: Level 1, Level 2, Level 3 and Level 4. Each of the four levels of care has a corresponding revenue code: 0171, 0172, 0173 and 0174, respectively. This policy outlines Humana’s billing requirements and reimbursement for NICU claims. Please note the definitions and background information for the following terms that are relevant for this policy: • Neonate: An infant who is less than four weeks old. • Prematurity: The condition when a neonate is born before a gestational age of 37 weeks and zero days. • Extreme prematurity: The condition when a neonate is born before a gestational age of 28 weeks and zero days. • Neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (RDS) (ICD-10-CM diagnosis code P22.0): Occurs when there is a deficiency of

surfactant. This is primarily due to insufficient production of surfactant or in rare cases, it can be caused by a genetic mutation in surfactant proteins or the transporter genes. Prematurity is the primary cause as surfactant production by the lungs does not occur until around a gestational age of 26 weeks, so the majority of cases are seen in the extreme premature

population. In total, all case-types of newborn respiratory distress occurs in approximately 7 percent of deliveries with only about 1 percent resulting in RDS. Prematurity and low birth weight are the most important risk factors in the development of RDS and usually occurs before a gestational age of 28 weeks. Chest X-ray findings for RDS are classic. The findings include diffuse atelectasis, with a ground-glass appearance, air bronchograms and low lung volumes. Treatment includes surfactant therapy; assisted ventilation with a ventilator, continuous positive airway pressure (regular or nasal), or other assisted ventilation such as high flow oxygen; monitoring of oxygenation; and supportive care (thermoregulation, nutritional support, fluid and electrolyte management, etc.) • Transient tachypnea of the newborn (ICD-10-CM diagnosis code P22.1): A transient respiratory distress caused when fetal lung fluid that is not readily absorbed from the lungs during the delivery process. Chest X-ray findings show lungs that are normal or hyperinflated. There is noted perihilar streaking, and the lung fissures can demonstrate fluid in them. Treatment is oxygen and supportive care. This typically resolves within a few days. • Other respiratory distress of newborn (ICD-10-CM diagnosis code P22.8): Respiratory distress that occurs in the neonatal period that is related to a specific disease process. Examples include respiratory distress secondary to pneumonia, sepsis, meconium aspiration, congenital heart defect, etc. • Respiratory distress of newborn, unspecified (ICD-10-CM diagnosis code P22.9): Respiratory distress that occurs in the neonatal period that is not related to a specific identified disease process or does not meet the definition of transient tachypnea of the newborn or RDS. sections.heading: Florida Medicaid Payment Policy
content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. To be reimbursed for a medically necessary NICU stay subject to DRG-based pricing, the provider must satisfy the requirements in this policy. During the NICU stay, the provider must provide all relevant documentation, such as medical records, for utilization management and leveling purposes. Humana uses all relevant documentation to assign the DRG for the case according to the table below. For a case that qualifies for more than one DRG, Humana assigns the DRG associated with the most complex services. Humana uses all relevant documentation to review the ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes reported on the claim according to the peer- reviewed literature definition and treatment requirements. If a reported diagnosis code does not satisfy the applicable requirement, it is not considered when calculating the DRG reimbursed. Humana reviews the level of care as reported by the NICU revenue code according to the table below. If the documentation associated with a charge for a NICU revenue code does not establish that the criteria associated with that revenue code were satisfied, reimbursement for the claim will instead be calculated using the highest NICU revenue code for which the criteria are satisfied.

Neonatal aftercare

Level 0 and Level 1 are considered newborn nursery.
Examples include care to observe for:
• Sepsis
• Temperature instability
• Feeding irregularities
• Jaundice

Neonate who is not severely ill but needs more hours of nursing and medical care than
typical neonates, as indicated by one or more of the following:
• Ventilatory support using one of the following:
- Hood oxygen, or
- Less than or equal to two liters per minute of oxygen via nasal cannula
• Administration of intravenous (IV) heplock medicines
• Weaning from nasogastric (NG) or nasojejunal (NJ) tube feedings while trying to
increase oral intake, without need for IV fluids
• Weaning from isolette or radiant warmer to open crib, without need for temperature
support
• Documented episodes of apnea, bradycardia or desaturation, for example:
- Apnea countdown,
- Titrating caffeine or preparing infant for home caffeine administration, or

- Preparing infant for home monitor use for apnea, bradycardia or desaturation
• Services for neonatal abstinence syndrome (NAS) when the Finnegan score is less
than or equal to 8
• Services for neonatal jaundice requiring either:
- Use of phototherapy, or
- Monitoring of bilirubin levels less frequently than every 12 hours
• Supportive care for growing premature infant, or establishing weight gain

Level 2 requirements are met
and
Temperature control modalities, such as isolette or radiant warmer, are in use
and
Condition requiring 6 to 12 hours of active nursing and medical evaluation, treatment and
support, as evidenced by one or more of the following:
• Ventilatory support using one of the following:
- Greater than two liters per minute of oxygen via nasal cannula,
- High flow nasal cannula,
- Continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP),
- Stable chronic mechanical ventilation (on home ventilator settings), or
- Conventional ventilator
• Umbilical venous catheter (UVC) or invasive cardiopulmonary monitoring (CPM)
• Hypoglycemia requiring D-10 bolus therapy
• Nothing by mouth (NPO) with either:
- All NG feedings, or
- Total parenteral nutrition (TPN)
• Services for NAS with one of the following:
- Three consecutive Finnegan scores greater than or equal to 8,
- Two consecutive Finnegan scores greater than or equal to 12, or
- Pharmacologic management of NAS

Level 3 requirements are met
and
Other condition that requires ongoing evaluation, active management, or therapy
adjustment with near continuous nursing and medical support, as evidenced by one or
more of the following:
• Ventilatory support using high frequency oscillating ventilator (HFOV)
• Use of IV bolus therapy, inotropic drugs, chronotropic drugs, calcium channel
blockers or IV prostaglandin therapy
• Active seizures, with need for anticonvulsants
• Surgical repair of severe congenital defect, for example:
- Omphalocele repair,
- Bowel resection for necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC), or
- Tracheoesophageal fistula repair
• Inhaled nitric oxide (iNO)
• Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO)
• Therapeutic cooling
• Hyperbilirubinemia requiring either:
- Exchange transfusion, or
- Intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) administration
• Emergent event (for example, pulmonary arrest or cardiac arrest)

sections.heading: Kentucky Medicaid Payment Policy
content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. To be reimbursed for a medically necessary NICU stay subject to DRG-based pricing, the provider must satisfy the requirements in this policy. During the NICU stay, the provider must provide all relevant documentation, such as medical records, for utilization management and leveling purposes. Humana uses all relevant documentation to assign the DRG for the case according to the table below. For a case that qualifies for more than one DRG as outlined in the table below, Humana assigns the DRG associated with the most complex services. Humana uses all relevant documentation to review the ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes reported on the claim according to the peer- reviewed literature definition and treatment requirements. If a reported diagnosis code does not satisfy the applicable requirement, it is not considered when calculating the DRG reimbursed. For a claim with a discharge date on or after May 29, 2025, Humana reviews additional factors to calculate reimbursement of the DRG outlier payment, when applicable, according to CMS MS-DRG guidelines. This includes reviewing whether the provider has billed for any days that do not meet medical necessity requirements. It also includes reviewing the following data on the claim: • The level of care as reported by the NICU revenue code, according to the applicable criteria established by MCG Health; • The number of days billed; and • The dates of service.

Neonatal aftercare

Level 0 and Level 1 are considered newborn nursery.
Examples include care to observe for:
• Sepsis
• Temperature instability
• Feeding irregularities
• Jaundice

Neonate who is not severely ill but needs more hours of nursing and medical care than
typical neonates, as indicated by one or more of the following:
• Ventilatory support using one of the following:
- Hood oxygen, or
- Less than or equal to two liters per minute of oxygen via nasal cannula
• Administration of intravenous (IV) heplock medicines
• Weaning from nasogastric (NG) or nasojejunal (NJ) tube feedings while trying to
increase oral intake, without need for IV fluids
• Weaning from isolette or radiant warmer to open crib, without need for temperature
support
• Documented episodes of apnea, bradycardia or desaturation, for example:
- Apnea countdown,
- Titrating caffeine or preparing infant for home caffeine administration, or
- Preparing infant for home monitor use for apnea, bradycardia or desaturation
• Services for neonatal abstinence syndrome (NAS) when the Finnegan score is less
than or equal to 8
• Services for neonatal jaundice requiring either:
- Use of phototherapy, or
- Monitoring of bilirubin levels less frequently than every 12 hours
• Supportive care for growing premature infant, or establishing weight gain

Level 2 requirements are met
and
Temperature control modalities, such as isolette or radiant warmer, are in use
and
Condition requiring 6 to 12 hours of active nursing and medical evaluation, treatment and
support, as evidenced by one or more of the following:
• Ventilatory support using one of the following:
- Greater than two liters per minute of oxygen via nasal cannula,
- High flow nasal cannula,
- Continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP),
- Stable chronic mechanical ventilation (on home ventilator settings), or
- Conventional ventilator
• Umbilical venous catheter (UVC) or invasive cardiopulmonary monitoring (CPM)
• Hypoglycemia requiring D-10 bolus therapy
• Nothing by mouth (NPO) with either:
- All NG feedings, or
- Total parenteral nutrition (TPN)
• Services for NAS with one of the following:
- Three consecutive Finnegan scores greater than or equal to 8,
- Two consecutive Finnegan scores greater than or equal to 12, or
- Pharmacologic management of NAS

Level 3 requirements are met
and
Other condition that requires ongoing evaluation, active management, or therapy
adjustment with near continuous nursing and medical support, as evidenced by one or
more of the following:
• Ventilatory support using high frequency oscillating ventilator (HFOV)
• Use of IV bolus therapy, inotropic drugs, chronotropic drugs, calcium channel
blockers or IV prostaglandin therapy
• Active seizures, with need for anticonvulsants
• Surgical repair of severe congenital defect, for example:
- Omphalocele repair,
- Bowel resection for necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC), or
- Tracheoesophageal fistula repair
• Inhaled nitric oxide (iNO)
• Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO)
• Therapeutic cooling
• Hyperbilirubinemia requiring either:
- Exchange transfusion, or
- Intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) administration
• Emergent event (for example, pulmonary arrest or cardiac arrest)

sections.heading: General Humana Resources
content: • Availity – Providers can register for access to information on a variety of topics such as eligibility, benefits, referrals, authorizations, claims and electronic remittances. • Claims processing edit notifications – Alerts of upcoming claims payment changes are posted on the first Friday of each month. • Claims resources – Providers can find information on referrals, authorizations, electronic claim submissions and more. • Making it easier – This page contains an educational series for providers and healthcare professionals. • Medical and pharmacy coverage policies – Humana publishes determinations of coverage of medical procedures, devices and medications for the treatment of various conditions. There may be variances in coverage among plans. • Publications – This page can help you find our quarterly newsletter, provider manual and other resources to help you do business with us. Note : Links to sources outside of Humana’s control are verified at the time of publication. Please report broken links .
